question: Can self-supervised learning be scaled to a 7B-parameter vision model on 1,689 million curated images while keeping dense feature maps good, giving one frozen backbone that beats specialised models?
hypothesis: Long-training degradation of dense features can be removed by regularising patch-similarity structure toward an early teacher, which unlocks scaling.
contributions: Data scaling with automatic curation mixed with retrieval and ImageNet data (LVD-1689M)
7B ViT with RoPE and constant hyperparameter schedules for 1M iterations
Gram anchoring against dense feature degradation
Post-hoc high-resolution adaptation, multi-student distillation into ViT and ConvNeXt family, text alignment

method.summary: DINOv3 scales DINOv2-style self-supervised learning to a 6.7B ViT trained on 1,689 million curated images for 1M iterations with constant hyperparameters. A Gram anchoring loss against an early teacher repairs dense features that degrade over long training; post-training adds high-resolution adaptation, single-teacher multi-student distillation to ViT and ConvNeXt models, and text alignment. Evaluated frozen on dense, global, video, 3D and satellite tasks.
method.task: self-supervised visual representation learning (vision foundation model)

models.name: DINOv3 ViT-7B/16
models.architecture: ViT with axial RoPE, 4 registers, SwiGLU FFN, patch size 16

other.rope_box_jitter: coordinate box [-1,1] scaled to [-s,s], s in [0.5,2]

models.name: DINOv3 ViT-S / S+ / B / L / H+
DINOv3 ConvNeXt T / S / B / L
Baselines: PEcore, PEspatial, SigLIP 2, AM-RADIOv2.5, Web-DINO 7B, Franca, AIMv2, EVA-CLIP-18B, V-JEPA 2, DINOv2

training.objective: L_Pre = L_DINO + L_iBOT + 0.1*L_DKoleo (Sinkhorn-Knopp centering); refinement L_Ref = wD*L_DINO + L_iBOT + wDK*L_DKoleo + wGram*L_Gram; L_Gram = ||X_S X_S^T - X_G X_G^T||_F^2 on L2-normalised patch features of global crops
training.lr_schedule: constant lr, weight decay and EMA momentum; linear warmup only for lr and teacher temperature; distilled students: 1M iterations then 250k iterations cosine lr cooldown
training.batch_size: 4096 images across 256 GPUs; 3.7M tokens per batch
training.steps: 1M iterations (7B pretraining); Gram refinement starts after 1M, teacher updated every 10k iterations, max 3 updates; 10k iterations high-res adaptation; satellite: 100k + 10k + 8k
training.seq_len: 2 global crops 256x256 and 8 local crops 112x112 (3.7M tokens per batch)
training.regularisation: Koleo on batches of 16; layer-wise lr decay 0.98; teacher EMA 0.999; masking ratio in [0.1,0.5] of global-crop patches with 50% probability
training.hardware: 256 GPUs, fully-sharded data parallel PyTorch; H100-SXM5 700W (Table 20)
training.compute: 61,440 GPU hours (ViT-7B), 47 MWh, 18 tCO2eq; whole project ~9M GPU hours, ~2600 tCO2eq

other.gram_teacher: early EMA teacher (100k or 200k iterations), input at 2x resolution then bicubic down-sample
other.text_alignment: dino.txt/LiT recipe: text encoder from scratch, vision frozen, 2 extra transformer layers, CLS concatenated with mean-pooled patches; hyperparameters not given
other.distillation: multi-student, teacher inference shared across all GPUs, GPU groups sized per student so iteration time matches; no Gram anchoring

inference.samples: single run per number; seeds not stated

parameters.video_tracking_best: context 7 frames, neighborhood 12 square, top-K 5, temperature 0.2 (Table 27 grid; best chosen on DAVIS train)

other.linear_probe_image: SGD momentum 0.9, 10 epochs, batch 1024, lr sweep 1e-4..5, wd {0,1e-5}
other.video_probe: 4 self-attention blocks + cross-attention, 16 frames, 256x256, 20 epochs, batch 64, lr {1e-4..5e-3}, wd {1e-3,1e-2,1e-1}
other.detection: Plain-DETR; AdamW wd 0.05; Objects365 22 ep batch 32 lr 5e-5 (/10 after ep 20), then 4 ep lr 2.5e-5 at 2048, then COCO 12 ep lr 2.5e-5 cosine to 2.5e-6; encoder 6 blocks dim 768, decoder 6 blocks, 1500+1500 queries; layers [10,20,30,40]; 3x3 windowing
other.segmentation: ViT-Adapter without injector + Mask2Former, dim 2048, batch 16, AdamW; COCO-Stuff 80k it lr 1.5e-5, Hypersim 10k it lr 2.5e-5, ADE20k 20k it lr 3e-5
other.depth: DPT head, frozen backbone, 1024x768, lr 1e-3 PolyLR power 3.5, warmup 12k it, 256 bins 0.001-100 m, dropout 0.05

limits: Weak on OCR-heavy tasks: authors say lacking image-text pairs, DINOv3 has a much harder time learning glyph associations and leave closing the gap to future work (App B.4).
Geographic fairness gaps remain (23% low- vs high-income, >14% Europe vs Africa).
Gram anchoring was applied late (after 1M iterations) and Gram teacher choice matters; no study of when it would be needed for smaller models (distilled students show no consistency issue).
Zero-shot global alignment slightly behind SigLIP 2 and PE (Sec 7.3).
No seeds, variance or significance reported; most ablations are single runs, some at 150k-200k iterations.
Training data from Instagram is not released, and wD, wDK loss weights are not given in the text.
Video SSv2 shows a dedicated video model (V-JEPA 2) ahead; DINOv3 ImageNet val trails SigLIP 2 / PE by 0.7-0.9.
Feature-dimension outliers appear in the 7B model; authors recommend final layer norm or batch norm for downstream use.
